questions.question: To see better when preparing to pass another vehicle on its left, you should:

options.text: Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Try to stand up on your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride on the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane when preparing to pass. This gives you a better view ahead and makes oncoming traffic see you better.

questions.question: During a normal turn, what should happen?

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
questions.explanation: The motorcycle and rider should lean together at the same angle during normal turns. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: When a group enters a curve, how should they ride?

options.text: Ride in a single-file line.
Ride in a staggered formation.
Ride in pairs.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.explanation: Switch to a single-file line when turning, taking curves, or entering or exiting a highway. This is safer than a staggered formation in these situations.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should travel:

options.text: Slower than you would during the day under the same conditions.
At the same speed you would travel during the day under the same conditions.
Faster than you would during the day under the same conditions.
On the shoulder of the road so other vehicles can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slower than you would during the day under the same conditions.
questions.explanation: Travel slower at night than you would during the day. It is hard to see hazards in the dark, so slowing down helps you avoid them.

questions.question: The body eliminates one drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are still in their body?

options.text: One drink
Two drinks
Three drinks
Four drinks

questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the total drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining in the body.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Always use both brakes.
Only use the front brake.
Only use the rear brake on wet pavement.
Only use the rear brake.

questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop, no matter what the road conditions are.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about hazards ahead.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.

options.text: Always
Usually
Frequently
Seldom

questions.explanation: You seldom hear a tire go flat on a motorcycle. You will notice a sudden change in how the bike handles instead.

questions.question: Face shields and goggles:

options.text: Will likely never need to be replaced.
Will scratch and become brittle over time and need regular replacement.
Should be made of breakable materials so they break away in a crash.
Should not allow air to pass through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will scratch and become brittle over time and need regular replacement.
questions.explanation: Plastic face shields and goggles scratch and become brittle as time passes. Replace them often to keep your eyes protected and your vision clear.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle operator stop other drivers from sharing their lane?

options.text: By giving dirty looks to other drivers
By riding in the center of the lane
By riding on the left side of the lane
By riding in a zigzag pattern

questions.correctAnswerText: By riding in the center of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane so there is not much space on either side of your motorcycle. This makes it harder for drivers to try to share the lane with you.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Keep your usual following distance.
Brake later than usual.
Ride a little slower than usual.
Ride a little faster than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride a little slower than usual.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle will sit lower with a passenger's extra weight. Ride slower than usual, especially through curves and over bumps. The extra weight makes your motorcycle slower to speed up, slow down, and stop. Keep more space between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: A good lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Help you see other vehicles and be seen.
Help you avoid road hazards.
Help you avoid traffic signals.
Show other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It helps you avoid wind, blind spots, and road hazards. It tells other drivers not to share your lane and gives you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: To be more visible at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Turn your headlight off.
Keep your headlight on.
Make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride very close to the car ahead.

questions.explanation: Keeping your headlight on is the best way to help other drivers see you at an intersection. Your headlight should be on whenever your motorcycle is running.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to weave over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Brake suddenly.
Steer side to side to match the weave.
Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.
Move to the left side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. If this happens, relax and ride straight ahead at the same speed. Weaving side to side to match the motion will only make it worse.

questions.question: When riding in fog, you should:

options.text: Use your high beam headlight.
Use your low beam headlight.
Use no lights.
Switch between high and low beams.

questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in fog. Do not use your high beams when other vehicles are near.

questions.question: When turning a corner:

options.text: You have less grip for braking.
You have more grip for braking.
Braking works the same as on a straight road.
You should never brake while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have less grip for braking.
questions.explanation: You can brake while turning, but be very careful. When leaning to turn, some of your tire grip is used for turning. This leaves less grip available for braking.

questions.question: On a long trip, you should:

options.text: Take as few rest breaks as possible.
Use caffeine or other stimulants if you feel sleepy.
Dress warmly to stay comfortable.
Ride more than 12 hours a day.

questions.explanation: Protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain to reduce fatigue. Limit riding to no more than six hours a day. Take a break at least every two hours. Do not use stimulants like caffeine because fatigue will hit hard when they wear off.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Only use your mirrors to check for other vehicles.
Turn your head to look for traffic behind you.
Not worry about other traffic.
Brake hard to let vehicles in your blind spot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to look for traffic behind you.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes.

questions.question: After a helmet has been in a crash, it should be:

options.text: Checked carefully.
Replaced.
Given to another rider.
Given a new chin strap.

questions.explanation: Replace any helmet that has been worn in a crash.

questions.question: A rider is well-protected when wearing:

options.text: A jacket that leaves the arms exposed.
Boots with high heels.
Leather gloves.
Shoes that stop below the ankle.

questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs fully. Choose boots or shoes that are tall and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles. Boots should have low heels so they do not catch on foot pegs or road surfaces. Leather gloves or gloves made of strong material protect your hands in a crash and give you a better grip on the controls.

questions.question: If you are riding next to another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up or slow down.
Wave at the other driver.
Stay alongside the vehicle until the next exit.
Let the other driver worry about it.

questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. You could be in the vehicle's blind spot. The vehicle could also block your escape route if danger appears. Speed up or slow down to move away from the vehicle.

questions.question: What happens to a sidecar when a motorcycle accelerates?

options.text: It feels like it is lagging behind.
It feels like it is accelerating faster than the motorcycle.
It vibrates uncontrollably.
It makes acceleration seem faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: It feels like it is lagging behind.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is an unpowered attachment. When you accelerate, it lags behind because of its weight and inertia.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black text. These signs tell drivers what rules to follow on the road.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane when preparing to pass a vehicle on the left?

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The center of the lane.
The right side of the lane.
Either the right or center portions of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane to pass safely on the left. This position gives you the best view of the road ahead.

questions.question: Where should you ride if hazards are on your left?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane to stay away from them. Adjust your position as conditions change.
